title: Generation-1 PolicyLM Continuous Multi-Objective Training (v1 / R21)
summary: Trained the 893,957-parameter PolicyLM over the 6,640-program v1 catalog using the unanchored 5-term L6 objective (CE + 0.5*BT + 0.5*listwise + 0.25*q-MSE + 0.1*runtime) for 17,773 updates across 40 continuation epochs.

data.splits_and_contexts: 6,982 train contexts (from 8,402 total harvested rows) and 263 held-out val contexts; 1,148 dev/test contexts excluded from updates
data.parent_clusters: 291 total lineage parent clusters across corpus
data.contamination_controls: R6 lineage split seal (14-step prefix + union-find parent clustering) + R5 inner-fold teacher target correction

arms_or_configs: v1 PolicyLM (d_model=128, 3-layer Transformer, 893,957 params) under unanchored L6 loss
ReduceLROnPlateau (patience=3 epochs, factor=0.5, floor=1e-6)
protocol.compute_budget: 429 initial updates + 17,344 continuation updates = 17,773 total optimizer steps across 40 epochs on single RTX 3090
protocol.evaluation_metric: Held-out 263-context validation L6 total loss and per-head component losses

outcome.verdict: Policy heads (CE, Bradley-Terry, listwise, runtime) converged cleanly by epoch 10 (-10.8% L6 reduction), but the neural outcome head (q-hat) failed to improve (0.1804 -> 0.1809) and LR decayed to the 1e-6 floor by step 5,677.
what_worked: Policy cross-entropy (-15.9%), Bradley-Terry (-6.6%), listwise (-5.2%), and runtime (-10.9%) heads all improved monotonically before plateauing.
Frozen checkpoint step-17344 (SHA-256 792f64c23da92bf7ed2f1b43f792a6a38219a79d52c1b0279eb7363aa4c0635d) provides a deterministic baseline prior.
what_failed: Outcome regression head (q-hat) stayed flat at ~0.1809 MSE across all 40 epochs.
31-epoch plateau after step 5,677 showed zero further gain from extra gradient steps on a static 6,640-program pool.
non_claims: Does not establish multi-round self-play improvement over an expanding vocabulary.
Does not validate q-hat as a useful candidate reranker.

next_experiment_implications: Decouple outcome prediction/selection from the PolicyLM q-hat head or replace with a calibrated tabular/GBDT/ridge selector.
Further epochs on a static pool yield zero return after ~6k steps; improvement requires vocabulary expansion + roundwise targets.

title: Outcome Head (q-hat) Pairwise Ranking, Best-of-8 Reranking, and GBDT Baseline Comparison
summary: Tested whether the PolicyLM neural outcome head (q-hat) can rank fresh sampled programs on 32 held-out development contexts (D5b) and compared neural outcome prediction against LightGBM on equal-lineage splits (DL_wave4).

data.splits_and_contexts: 32 kept development contexts (D5b) for fresh-program ranking; equal-lineage held-out splits (DL_wave4) for neural vs. LightGBM R^2 comparison
data.parent_clusters: Lineage-grouped evaluation across kept development contexts
data.candidate_or_catalog_size: 32 fresh policy-sampled programs per context (reranked to top-8) vs. 8 direct policy samples
data.contamination_controls: Evaluated strictly on held-out development contexts; fresh candidate draws

arms_or_configs: Arm A: Direct top-8 policy sampling without q-hat reranking
Arm B: Sample 32 from PolicyLM, select top-8 by q-hat prediction
Arm C (DL_wave4): Neural outcome predictor vs. LightGBM regressor on equal-lineage splits
protocol.compute_budget: Offline CPU/GPU evaluation across 32 contexts x 32 program draws + DL_wave4 cross-validation
protocol.evaluation_metric: Pairwise concordance accuracy, paired dScore / dBestQ (bootstrap 95% CI), and held-out R^2

outcome.verdict: NEGATIVE / INCONCLUSIVE for neural q-hat: pairwise accuracy on fresh programs is 0.506 (indistinguishable from 0.50 coin flip), 32->8 reranking is statistically indistinguishable from zero, and the neural predictor trails LightGBM by -0.095 R^2.
what_worked: LightGBM achieved R^2 = 0.785 on equal-lineage outcome prediction, outperforming the neural predictor by +0.095 R^2 (95% CI [+0.056, +0.133]).
what_failed: Neural q-hat pairwise ranking on fresh programs is chance-level (0.506 [0.441, 0.568]).
Best-of-8 from 32 q-hat reranking produced no significant gain over plain policy sampling (dScore +0.031 [-0.0625, +0.125]).
non_claims: q-hat cannot be claimed as an active value critic or candidate filter.

next_experiment_implications: Disable q-hat reranking in policy inference until a validated tabular/ridge/GBDT selector replaces it.
Benchmark simple linear/ridge and GBDT selectors directly on frozen candidate pools under cluster-grouped CV (H2).

title: Best-of-8 Development Panel Matches: Teacher vs. PolicyLM vs. Uniform Catalog Sampling
summary: Compared best-of-8 candidate draws from the teacher pool, frozen v1 PolicyLM, PolicyLM + q-rerank, and uniform random catalog sampling across 32 development contexts.

data.parent_clusters: 32 contexts sampled prior to full R6 split seal
data.candidate_or_catalog_size: 8 evaluated programs per context drawn from the 6,640-program catalog
data.contamination_controls: PRELIMINARY: T1/D5b matches were launched before the R6 lineage split seal landed; reported as directional only

arms_or_configs: teacher (historical pool oracle upper bound)
uniform (8 uniform random draws from 6,640 catalog)
policy (8 draws from frozen v1 PolicyLM)
policy_plus_q_rerank (top-8 by q-hat from 32 PolicyLM draws)
protocol.compute_budget: 32 contexts x 8 program evaluations per arm
protocol.evaluation_metric: Mean best-of-8 normalized task score and regret relative to teacher

outcome.verdict: PolicyLM sampling closes 76% of the gap between uniform catalog draws and the teacher oracle (regret 0.140 vs. 0.591, a 4.2x regret reduction), but remains preliminary because T1/D5b preceded the R6 lineage split seal.
what_worked: PolicyLM prior concentrates probability mass on high-performing programs far better than uniform catalog draws (1.994 vs. 1.542).
what_failed: Pre-R6 split provenance prevents using T1/D5b as a leakage-free outer-split claim.
non_claims: Directional development evidence only; not a sealed post-R6 outer-test benchmark claim.

next_experiment_implications: Re-run matched best-of-k comparisons on post-R6 lineage-sealed held-out clusters with >= 24 parent clusters.

title: C7 Evaluator Parity Census: Native Evaluator vs. Emitted Rust Source Across 1,554 Proposals
summary: Audited prediction parity between the in-memory native AST evaluator and emitted standalone Rust code across the 6,640-program catalog and 1,554 harvested proposals.

data.splits_and_contexts: 1,554 harvested candidate program proposals across the 6,640-program v1 catalog
data.candidate_or_catalog_size: 6,640 catalog programs (1,073 containing quantile_bin); 1,554 evaluated proposals (342 with quantile_bin, 1,212 without quantile_bin)
data.contamination_controls: Deterministic synthetic and harvested input matrices

arms_or_configs: In-memory native Rust AST evaluator vs. emitted standalone Rust source compiled and executed on identical inputs
protocol.evaluation_metric: Exact prediction agreement rate (overall, quantile-containing, and non-quantile subsets)

outcome.verdict: 100% of the 41/1,554 (2.64%) parity failures in the v1 catalog census occurred in programs using quantile_bin due to tie-breaking at bin boundaries; 0/1,212 non-quantile programs failed.
what_worked: 1,212/1,212 (100%) parity across all v1 catalog proposals without quantile_bin.
Isolated exact root cause of the 41 failures to quantile threshold tie-breaking.
what_failed: 11.99% (41/342) of quantile-containing proposals diverged at bin edges.
non_claims: Does not cover out-of-catalog GP mutations introducing extreme log1p/div domain edge cases (see EXP-008).

next_experiment_implications: Enforce canonical mid-rank quantile tie-breaking and strict domain clamping for div/log1p in both native and emitted evaluators.

title: v2 Trainer Build Qualification: R23 (L6 + 0.2*KL) Bitwise Parity and 230-Fixture Gate
summary: Verified that the refactored continuous_v6 (v2) trainer reproduces the R23 (L6 + 0.2*KL) next-update loss and post-step weights bitwise across 8 GPU runs and passes 230 offline CPU fixtures.

data.splits_and_contexts: Pinned step-17344 checkpoint + deterministic R22 batch fixture + 230 offline CPU verification fixtures
data.contamination_controls: Offline fixture verification only; zero production S3 writes

arms_or_configs: 8 repeated GPU next-update receipts under continuous_v6 (L6 + 0.2*KL)
2-step CPU dry run + 3-step GPU dry run + 230 offline CPU fixtures
protocol.compute_budget: 8 GPU single-step parity runs + 230 CPU test fixtures
protocol.evaluation_metric: Exact IEEE-754 float32 loss match and post-step parameter tensor mismatch count

outcome.verdict: Build and numerical determinism qualified: all 8 GPU runs produced identical loss 0.9540845 with 0 tensor mismatches across 893,957 parameters.
what_worked: Bitwise reproducible gradient updates on GPU under L6 + 0.2*KL.
230/230 offline CPU contract fixtures passed.
what_failed: Build qualification does not itself prevent held-out lineage forgetting during multi-epoch continuation (see EXP-007).
non_claims: Qualifies build/mechanics only; not a live learning-loop improvement claim.

next_experiment_implications: Pair bitwise-verified trainer mechanics with full-corpus lineage coverage and decomposed KL guards before live multi-round updates.

title: R22 GPU Scratch Sweeps (3, 4a, 4b, 5, 6): KL Anchoring and L_PI Objective Trade-Off
summary: Executed five 8-epoch GPU scratch sweeps from frozen v1 on the R22 corpus (with 885 training contexts held out) to test 0.2*KL anchoring and policy-improvement loss weights lambda_PI in {0.01, 0.03, 0.10}.

data.splits_and_contexts: 1,636 kept R22 contexts partitioned into 488 active train, 263 val, and 885 held-out train contexts (221 parent clusters)
data.parent_clusters: 291 total parent clusters (221 in the 885 held-out train subset)
data.contamination_controls: Scratch sweeps isolated from production S3 checkpoints; evaluated on 263 val and 885 held-out train contexts

arms_or_configs: Sweep 3: unanchored L6
Sweep 4a: L6 + 0.2*KL
Sweep 4b: L6 + 0.2*KL + 0.10*L_PI
Sweep 5: L6 + 0.2*KL + 0.01*L_PI
Sweep 6: L6 + 0.2*KL + 0.03*L_PI
protocol.evaluation_metric: Probe KL drift vs. frozen v1, held-out L_PI loss, held-out L6 loss, and paired checkpoint judge

outcome.verdict: NON-QUALIFYING diagnostic finding: 0.2*KL successfully bounds probe KL drift (<= 0.014 over 8 epochs vs. 0.052+ by epoch 2 unanchored), but adding L_PI creates a strict Pareto conflict—improving held-out L_PI (7.080 -> 6.59-6.87) while degrading held-out L6 (0.8610 -> 0.8621-0.8660).
what_worked: 0.2*KL forward-KL anchor reduced 8-epoch policy drift by >3.7x (<= 0.014 vs. >= 0.052).
what_failed: All L_PI weights (0.01, 0.03, 0.10) degraded composite L6 loss on held-out contexts.
263-context val panel alone was underpowered to resolve small paired differences.
non_claims: Scratch diagnostic sweeps only; no checkpoint promoted.

next_experiment_implications: Drop composite L_PI auxiliary loss or align the judge metric directly with roundwise best-of-k task loss.
Power paired checkpoint evaluations using the combined 1,148-context judge (263 val + 885 held-out train).

title: R25/R26/R27 kNN Prior Sweeps and 1,148-Context Paired Judge Regression Discovery
summary: Tested kNN neighborhood cross-entropy regularization (R25 lambda=0.25, R26 replicate, R27 lambda=0.05) against r25control (L6 + 0.2*KL) and evaluated checkpoints on the first adequately powered 1,148-context paired judge.

data.splits_and_contexts: Trained on 488 active train contexts; judged on 1,148 held-out contexts (263 val + 885 held-out train lineages)
data.parent_clusters: 221 parent clusters in the 885 held-out train subset + 70 val clusters
data.contamination_controls: Paired bootstrap over parent clusters on 1,148 contexts disjoint from the 488 active update contexts

arms_or_configs: r25control: L6 + 0.2*KL (no kNN term)
R26: seed replicate of R25
protocol.compute_budget: 4 GPU scratch runs x 4-8 epochs + 1,148-context paired cluster-bootstrap judge
protocol.evaluation_metric: Paired delta L6 vs. frozen v1 on 1,148 contexts (95% cluster-bootstrap CI) and probe KL

outcome.verdict: REGRESSION ALERT on all 3 judged checkpoints: while the 263 val contexts looked flat (-0.0001 to -0.0005), the 885 held-out train lineages degraded by +0.0042 to +0.0063 L6, proving that updating on a 488-context subset induces distribution-shift forgetting on unvisited lineages even under 0.2*KL.
what_worked: The KL freeze guard caught R25's 0.1079 KL spike at epoch 1 and halted further drift.
Expanding the judge from 263 to 1,148 contexts shrank CI width ~2.1x and exposed cross-lineage forgetting that 263 val missed.
what_failed: Updating on 488 contexts degraded L6 on the 885 unvisited train lineages across every arm (including r25control +0.00310).
0.25*CE_kNN caused immediate KL explosion (0.1079 at epoch 1).
non_claims: All checkpoints rejected by regression gate; frozen v1 remains undefeated on the 1,148-context judge.

next_experiment_implications: Never train continuation updates on a narrow subset of lineages without replay or full-corpus coverage (EI-1: test r25control on all 1,636 contexts).
Always stratify evaluation across >= 24 parent clusters and include unvisited lineage probes.

title: GB-06 / H1 Bounded GP Vocabulary Expansion Pilot on xbabe3 (24 Contexts x 3 Arms)
summary: Ran a real-budget 3-arm genetic programming pilot (ordinary GP vs. frozen-v1 policy_seeded GP vs. training-only retrieval_seeded GP) across 24 frozen training contexts on xbabe3 with a 512-fit cap per arm.

data.splits_and_contexts: 24 frozen training contexts (19 classification, 5 regression); 17/24 complete-case contexts across all 3 arms, 18/24 with >= 1 completed arm
data.candidate_or_catalog_size: Up to 512 GP candidate evaluations per context-arm (pop=32, gen=15); 51 valid completed arm champions inspected against the 6,640-program v1 catalog
data.contamination_controls: Strictly training-only context manifests; retrieval_seeded restricted to training contexts with target dataset excluded

arms_or_configs: ordinary: baseline GP evolution from default initial population
policy_seeded: GP initial population seeded from frozen v1 PolicyLM (step-17344)
retrieval_seeded: GP initial population seeded from historical best training-only program on nearest neighbor dataset
protocol.compute_budget: 512 candidate fits/arm cap, 900s per-arm wall-clock cap, 4-hour total campaign cap on xbabe3 CPU (53 completed arm receipts, 18 interrupted at deadline)
protocol.evaluation_metric: Paired complete-case champion validation loss (log_loss_ratio = ln(loss_a / loss_b)), novel out-of-catalog champion rate, and native-vs-Rust parity

outcome.verdict: NON-QUALIFYING pilot with two decisive discoveries: (1) retrieval_seeded GP crushed ordinary GP (16 wins, 1 tie, 0 losses; median log-loss ratio -0.0354), whereas frozen v1 policy_seeded GP gave negligible median gain (-0.000349) and lost badly on outlier ctx-001279 (3.081 vs. 0.675); (2) 40/51 (78.4%) GP champions were genuinely novel ASTs outside the 6,640 catalog.
what_worked: Retrieval-seeded GP won 16/17 complete contexts against ordinary GP (0 losses) and 13/17 against policy-seeded GP.
GP mutation/crossover discovered 40/51 champions outside the static 6,640-program v1 vocabulary.
48/51 valid champions achieved bitwise native-vs-emitted Rust parity.
what_failed: Frozen v1 policy_seeded GP showed near-zero median advantage over ordinary GP (-0.000349) and suffered catastrophic prior mismatch on ctx-001279.
18/72 arm runs hit the 900s wall-clock cap on wider datasets (6/24 contexts incomplete).
3/51 champions failed native-vs-Rust parity (1 regression AST using log1p/div; 2 classification ASTs using div).
non_claims: Single-round training-split pilot with 6 incomplete contexts and 3 parity failures; does not qualify H1 or multi-round self-play.

next_experiment_implications: Seed multi-round GP with a hybrid retrieval + policy population rather than frozen v1 PolicyLM draws alone.
Fix the 3 div/log1p native-vs-emitted Rust parity discrepancies before launching Round-1 self-play.
Bound per-evaluation row/feature work or adapt timeout budgets so wider datasets do not censor 25% of contexts.

title: CLOVER Phase 2/3 Host Readout (J9): Frozen-Pool Selector Audit and 5-Round Offline Distillation
summary: Executed the offline CLOVER Phase 2/3 host pipeline (jope_pools + jope_retention) across 1,222 frozen candidate pools (21,199 rows) and 8,908 distilled S3 GP index rows over 5 rounds.

data.splits_and_contexts: 1,382 kept R22 contexts -> 1,222 valid frozen pools (864 train, 180 val, 178 test; 21,199 candidate rows) + 8,908 S3 GP index rows (426 programs across 10 datasets)
data.parent_clusters: Lineage-grouped train/val/test split over 1,222 frozen pools
data.candidate_or_catalog_size: 21,199 candidate evaluation rows in frozen pools; 8,908 rows / 426 programs in S3 GP index
data.contamination_controls: Strict split isolation verified by jope_pools export and evaluate

arms_or_configs: Phase 2 selector tournament on 1,222 frozen pools (eval_budgets = [1, 4, 8], bootstrap = 1,000)
Phase 3 5-round offline flywheel-distill on 8,908 S3 GP index rows (eval_budgets = [1, 4, 8])
Debug vs. Release binary runtime profiling
protocol.compute_budget: Release CPU execution on xbabe2: 44s for evaluate (down from 767s debug) and 558s for flywheel-distill (down from 8,125s debug)
protocol.evaluation_metric: Top-k regret on frozen pools, strongest baseline comparison, and flywheel_established verdict

outcome.verdict: NON-QUALIFYING negative result on complex learned selectors: simple ridge_program remained the strongest baseline on the 1,222 frozen pools (ranking_learnability: NOT_ESTABLISHED), and offline 5-round replay on static S3 GP index rows returned flywheel_established: false. Release builds cut runtime by 14.6x-17.4x.
what_worked: Release compilation (--release) accelerated jope_pools evaluate by 17.4x (767s -> 44s) and flywheel-distill by 14.6x (8,125s -> 558s).
Automated fail-closed verdicts prevented overclaiming when complex selectors failed to beat ridge_program.
what_failed: Learned complex selectors did not beat ridge_program on held-out frozen pools.
Offline replay over static S3 GP index rows cannot substitute for live roundwise GP generation and refitting.
non_claims: Does not establish H2 ranking learnability or H3 flywheel lift.

next_experiment_implications: Adopt ridge_program (and test compact GBDT/empirical-Bayes shrinkage with rich program+dataset features) as the default fast filter instead of complex neural value heads.
Test H3 on true live multi-round GP generation (SPQ-1 protocol) rather than static offline index replay.

title: Core-IP Bounded 1-Hour GPU End-to-End Latency Window (step-60000 Policy)
summary: Attempted a bounded 1-hour RTX 3090 end-to-end latency benchmark across 10 datasets using the step-60000 policy checkpoint, which halted in 428ms on a pre-existing window.json receipt guard.

data.splits_and_contexts: 10 benchmark datasets (adult, airlines, albert, bank-marketing, california, covertype, credit, default-of-credit-card-clients, eye_movements, higgs)
data.candidate_or_catalog_size: step-60000 policy checkpoint + 20-generation GP search budget

arms_or_configs: 1-hour bounded GPU controller run on RTX 3090 (24 GB VRAM)
protocol.compute_budget: Planned 3,600s GPU window; actual execution 428ms before fail-closed abort
protocol.evaluation_metric: Per-dataset wall-clock latency and task loss

outcome.verdict: FAILED BEFORE EXECUTION: controller aborted after 428ms because window.json already existed in the output directory and staging input-boundary checks flagged a path mismatch. Fixed in v3 timing-window contract.
what_worked: Fail-closed receipt guard prevented overwriting prior benchmark evidence.
what_failed: Zero datasets were timed in the GPU window due to output-path collision.
non_claims: Zero GPU latency measurements produced in this window.

next_experiment_implications: Use unique timestamped output directories and preflight input-boundary verification (v3 contract) before dispatching any GPU window.

title: Deterministic Same-Cut 10-Dataset Benchmark and SOTArena 52,329-Entry Elo Replay
summary: Verified deterministic reproduction of the 10-dataset same-cut benchmark (273s CPU) and byte-identical replay of the 52,329-entry SOTArena Elo ladder.

data.splits_and_contexts: 10 same-cut tabular benchmark datasets; 52,329 historical evaluation entries in SOTArena registry
data.parent_clusters: 10 benchmark families (same-cut) and historical SOTArena registry
data.candidate_or_catalog_size: 52,329 registry entries across 15 tracked model families

arms_or_configs: Same-cut 10-dataset benchmark runner
jope-arena elo --check deterministic Elo ladder replay
protocol.compute_budget: 273s CPU wall-clock for 10-dataset same-cut benchmark; <5s for Elo replay check
protocol.evaluation_metric: Byte-identical Elo leaderboard reproduction and per-dataset wall-clock completion

outcome.verdict: ESTABLISHED infrastructure and descriptive baseline: both the 273s 10-dataset same-cut runner and the 52,329-entry Elo replay are deterministic and byte-identical.
what_worked: Fast (273s), reproducible 10-dataset CPU benchmark baseline.
Byte-identical verification of historical Elo ratings in CI.
what_failed: Historical SOTArena registry aggregates heterogeneous splits/budgets and cannot be used alone as a controlled H4 proof.

title: SPQ-1 Self-Play Round Qualification Verifier and Round-1 Equal-Budget Preregistration
summary: Implemented and verified the fail-closed SPQ-1 round qualification verifier (jope.selfplay-round-qualification/v1) and froze the Round-1 preregistration comparing a 4-round self-play ratchet (4x16 fits) against single-round ordinary GP (1x64 fits) at equal total budget B_total = 64.

data.splits_and_contexts: Preregistered for >= 24 held-out parent clusters (disjoint from all training/seeding lineages); verified on synthetic passing and failing regression fixtures
data.parent_clusters: Minimum 24 independent parent clusters required for qualification
data.candidate_or_catalog_size: B_total = 64 candidate fits per context (Arm A: 1x64 ordinary GP; Arm B: K=4 rounds x 16 fits with roundwise distillation and catalog growth)
data.contamination_controls: Enforces train_val_disjoint, outer_test_disjoint, meta_test_disjoint, program_digest SHA-256 verification, and create-only receipt emission

arms_or_configs: Arm A (single_round_ordinary_gp): 1 round x 64 candidate evaluations
Arm B (multi_round_selfplay_ratchet): K = 4 rounds x 16 candidate evaluations with roundwise vocabulary expansion and decomposed KL guard
protocol.compute_budget: Equal total candidate evaluation budget B_total = 64 per context; verifier runs in <1s offline on CPU (8 dedicated contract tests, 5,006 total workspace Rust tests)
protocol.evaluation_metric: Cluster-level mean log-loss ratio ln(L_multi / L_single) <= -0.01 with one-sided 97.5% upper CI < 0 (alpha = 0.025), monotonic round non-degradation, and decomposed KL guard (conditional_base_kl <= 0.20, new_support_mass <= 0.15)

outcome.verdict: DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY / PREREGISTERED: The SPQ-1 verifier and Round-1 preregistration are merged to main (PR #343, commit c402b2118) with full chain-rule KL decomposition, derived admissibility, and fail-closed rubric checks; live Round-1 compute execution is pending.
what_worked: Solved the expanding-vocabulary KL problem by decomposing total KL into conditional_base_kl (<= 0.20) on shared base support plus new_support_mass (<= 0.15) on novel GP programs.
Enforced strict fail-closed verification on probability mass conservation, chain-rule KL identity, derived admissibility, and parent-cluster bootstrap CIs.
what_failed: Live Round-1 campaign has not yet been executed on the >= 24 held-out parent clusters.
non_claims: Offline verifier and preregistration only; zero live self-play lift claimed until Round-1 executes and passes.

next_experiment_implications: Execute Round-1 (EXP-NEXT-02) under selfplay-round1-prereg.v1.json using hybrid retrieval+policy seeding after closing the 3 div/log1p parity bugs from EXP-008.
